scrutiny.test: T0 purpose: prismis is a local-first tool that runs unattended on the operator's hosts (docs/IDEA.md); this keeps it on the interpreter the hosts already run and makes production run what the gate tested.
scrutiny.failureCase: The move left production on unverified dependency versions.

scrutiny.test: T1 owners: .python-version is what uv run reads, so verify.sh and CI follow it (neither names a version); the prior decision at docs/architecture/decisions.md:277 owns install-time pinning and is extended, not contradicted.
scrutiny.failureCase: A second place that decides the interpreter, or a pinning rule weaker than the existing one.

scrutiny.test: T2 same noun: the 3.14 proof is the full suites run on 3.14.6 against the refreshed locks (980 and 126 passed); the production comparison read cerebro's installed tool environment with uv pip list, not the lock.
scrutiny.failureCase: A wheel's existence taken as proof it works.

scrutiny.test: T3 degrade: a deploy now fails when the lock cannot be satisfied instead of resolving something else, and 3.13 stays installed until the operator removes it; both stated as sacrifices.
T4 reuse: the existing install targets, the uv python guard and test_dep_pin_unit.py are extended; `uv export` plus `uv tool install --constraints` are uv's own primitives.
T5 running system: commitment 4 installs into a scratch tool directory and compares installed versions to the lock; commitment 6 is cerebro's deployed fetch cycle on 3.14.

T6 assumptions checked: uv tool install accepts -c/--constraints (its --help); the CLI's lock carries an editable path entry for prismis-daemon (cli/pyproject.toml:69), so the export drops it by name.
scrutiny.failureCase: A constraints file uv refuses at deploy time.

scrutiny.test: T7 consumers, enumerated with grep: install-binaries depends on install-daemon and install-cli-local (Makefile:83); cerebro's deploy runs make install-daemon and make install-cli-local; nothing else installs prismis.
T9 six months: the version lives once per unit in .python-version; a test fails if the Makefile hardcodes it again or drops the constraints.
T10 reversibility: a revert reinstalls on 3.13 with the old locks; no data or schema change.
scrutiny.failureCase: A one-way change resting on reasoning.

scrutiny.test: T11 class, swept with grep for uv tool install, uv python install and 3.13 over *.md, Makefile, *.sh, *.yml and *.toml: every prismis install and interpreter pin is in the Makefile, the two .python-version files and the two mypy settings; the README's lspeak lines install a separate tool. Go (the TUI) pins its own toolchain in tui/go.mod and is untouched. Engines axis n/a.
scrutiny.failureCase: A pin or unpinned install left elsewhere.

scrutiny.test: T13 two places: today the version is written in eight Makefile spots plus .python-version; after, once per unit.
T18 cause: the cause of production drift is the install resolving fresh; passing the lock as constraints removes it for every dependency, where the prior fix covered git sources only.
scrutiny.failureCase: A fix that pins only the packages that happened to drift.

scrutiny.test: T20 walk: on cerebro, `git pull && make install-daemon` reads 3.14 from daemon/.python-version, installs CPython 3.14 if missing, exports the lock to a temp constraints file, installs prismis-daemon with it, restarts; `uv pip list` on the tool env then matches the lock; `prismis-daemon verify` passes; the next cycle runs.
scrutiny.failureCase: A step that only works from a developer shell.
